activities.caption: bet first — tilt the hand further
activities.name: aeHandPredict

config.q: You tilt your flat hand further upward out of the car window. What happens to the two forces?
choices: Both increase — the push grows and tilts more upward, but backward too
Lift increases while drag vanishes — steeper means slipperier
Both decrease — a steeper hand slides through the air
config.why: Tilt more and the air pushes harder and more steeply: lift grows, and so does the backward component. Drag is the price that arrives with every extra degree.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — continuity is bookkeeping for mass
activities.name: aeContinuityCloze

config.text: Continuity says area × %%0%% = constant: same volume per second through a smaller hole means faster flow. The wind-tunnel duct of 0.1 m² fed at 10 m/s narrows to 0.05 m², so the speed doubles to %%1%% m/s.
config.hint: Squeeze the garden hose and the jet quickens — same water per second, smaller exit.

activities.anchor: lower pressure than the still air below
activities.caption: rebuild the wing's two-bookkeeping chain
activities.name: aeChainOrder

config.prompt: From shape to lift — put the chain in order:
items: The wing's curved top squeezes the streamlines together
Continuity speeds the air up over the top
Bernoulli drops the pressure where the flow sped up
Suction on the upper surface supplies about two-thirds of the lift
Newton's third law: the air deflected downward shoves the wing up
config.why: Two bookkeepings of one fact — suction above and deflection below are the same lift counted twice.

activities.caption: file the explanations — real physics or the transit-time myth?
activities.name: aeMythBuckets

config.prompt: Two rival stories about lift are in circulation. File each claim:

items.label: the air is deflected downward, so the wing is pushed up
suction over the curved upper surface pulls the wing up
two particles splitting at the leading edge must reunite at the trailing edge
the upper flow is faster because the shape and circulation impose it
a flat plate at an angle cannot generate lift

config.why: Nothing enforces a rendezvous: measurements show the upper particle arrives far earlier. The myth predicts no lift for a flat plate — which demonstrably flies.

activities.caption: pair each design lever with who pulls it
activities.name: aeLeverMatch

config.prompt: L = ½ρV²S·C_L: every letter is a design lever. Match the lever to the aircraft that pulls it:

pairs.right: gliders — slow flight buys lift with area
fighters — fast flight does the work, small wings suffice
airliners at cruise — heavier by far, buying lift in thinner air
the safety margin — comfortably below the stall ceiling

config.why: At 80 m/s, a 30 m² wing at C_L = 0.8 makes about 94,000 N — enough for roughly 9.6 tonnes.

activities.anchor: converge to within a few knots
activities.caption: call the magnitude — how thin is cruise air?
activities.name: aeDensityEstimate

config.prompt: Airliners cruise near 11,000 metres, where density is about 0.4 kg per cubic metre. Roughly what per cent of sea-level density (1.225 kg/m³) is that?
config.why: 0.4 ÷ 1.225 ≈ 33% — thin air is cheap air: drag falls with the same ½ρV² that lift does, so the aircraft simply flies faster.
config.context: But not too slowly, or the C_L it needs would cross the stall ceiling — hence coffin corner.

activities.caption: true or false — rival stories or one physics?
activities.name: aeLedgerJudge

statements.s: Bernoulli and Newton tell rival stories about lift — one must be wrong.
statements.why: They are the same physics counted twice: a pressure difference integrated over the wing, and air deflected downward.

statements.s: Wingtip vortices spiralling behind a landing airliner are the lift's downward momentum made visible.
statements.why: An aircraft flying level throws air downward continuously — on a humid day you can watch it.

statements.s: Air must arrive in step above and below the wing.
statements.why: Nothing enforces the rendezvous; the upper particle arrives far earlier.

statements.s: The Kutta–Joukowski theorem is a rival theory to the momentum view.
statements.why: It is the momentum view rewritten in the language engineers can compute with.
